Thermax Limited  �  Annual Report 2025-26Notes:
1.  The Explanatory Statement pursuant to Section 
102(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) in 
respect of the special business, is annexed hereto. 
Additional information in respect of Director seeking 
appointment/re-appointment at the 45th Annual 
General Meeting forms part of Explanatory Statement 
annexed to the notice.
2.  The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) in 
continuation to its General Circular No. 20/2020 dated 
May 5, 2020, Circular No. 02/2022 dated May 5, 2022, 
Circular No. 10/2022 dated December 28, 2022, 
Circular No. 09/2023 dated September 25, 2023, 
Circular No. 09/2024 dated September 19, 2024 and 
vide its Circular No. 03/2025 dated September 9, 2025 
in relation to “Clarification on holding of Annual General 
Meeting (AGM) and Extraordinary General Meeting 
(EGM) through Video Conferencing (VC) or Other 
Audio-Visual Means (OAVM)” (collectively referred to 
as “MCA Circulars”) has permitted the holding of AGM, 
without the physical presence of the Members at a 
common venue. In compliance with the MCA Circulars, 
the 45th AGM of the members of the Company is 
being held through VC/OAVM. The registered office 
of the Company shall be deemed to be the venue for 
the AGM.
3.  Since this AGM is being held pursuant to the aforesaid 
MCA Circulars through VC/OAVM, physical attendance 
of Members has been dispensed with. Accordingly, 
the facility for appointment of proxies by the Members 
will not be available for the AGM and hence the Proxy 
Form, Attendance Slip, and road map are not annexed 
to this Notice. The recorded transcript of the AGM shall 
also be made available on the website of the Company 
at www.thermaxglobal.com  within the prescribed time 
after the conclusion of the AGM.
4.  Members attending the AGM through VC/OAVM shall 
be counted for the purpose of reckoning the quorum 
under Section 103 of the Act.
5.  In compliance with the aforesaid MCA Circulars and 
the SEBI Circulars, Notice of the AGM along with 
the Annual Report for FY 2025-26 is being sent only 
through electronic mode to those Members whose 
email addresses are registered with the Company/
Depositories. Members may note that the Notice and 
Annual Report for FY 2025-26 will also be available 
on the Company’s website www.thermaxglobal.com  
and websites of the Stock Exchanges i.e. BSE Limited 
and National Stock Exchange of India Limited at www.
bseindia.com  and www.nseindia.com  respectively. The Company will also publish an advertisement in 
newspaper containing the details about the AGM i.e. 
the conduct of AGM through VC/OAVM, date and 
time of AGM, availability of notice of the AGM at the 
Company’s website on www.thermaxglobal.com  
and manner of registering the e-mail IDs of those 
shareholders who have not registered their email 
addresses with the Company/RTA.
6.  In compliance with Regulation 36(1)(b) of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”), a letter 
providing details of web-link, including the exact path, 
where complete details of the Annual Report are 
available is being sent to those shareholders whose 
email addresses are not registered with the Company/
RTA or with any depository.
7.  The statutory registers that are required to be kept 
open during the AGM and the documents that are 
referred to as available for inspection, in the notice 
or explanatory statement, shall be made available for 
inspection electronically on the date of the AGM. The 
members desiring to inspect the said documents shall 
contact cservice@thermaxglobal.com  on or before 
July 30, 2026.
8.  Procedure for Remote E-Voting and E-Voting at 
the AGM is as follows:
A.  Remote E-Voting (Voting through Electronic 
means):
 i.  In compliance with the provisions of Section 108 
of the Act, read with Rule 20 of the Companies 
(Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, 
as amended from time to time, Regulation 44 
of the Listing Regulations and in terms of SEBI 
circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD/CIR/P/2020/242 
dated December 9, 2020 in relation to e-Voting 
Facility Provided by Listed Entities, the Members 
are provided with the facility to cast their vote 
electronically, through the e-Voting services 
provided by KFintech, on all the resolutions set 
forth in this Notice. The instructions for e-Voting 
are given herein below.
 ii.  However, pursuant to SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/
CFD/CMD/CIR/P/2020/242 dated December 
9, 2020 on “e-Voting facility provided by Listed 
Companies”, e-Voting process has been enabled 
to all the individual demat account holders, by 
way of single login credential, through their demat 
accounts/websites of Depositories/DPs in order 
to increase the efficiency of the voting process.

I)  Login method for remote e-Voting for Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode:
Type of shareholders Login Method
Individual Shareholders 
holding securities in 
demat mode with NSDL1. Members already registered for IDeAS facility:
 I. Visit URL: https://eservices.nsdl.com
 II. Click on the “Beneficial Owner” icon under “Login” under ‘IDeAS’ section.
 III.  On the new page, enter User ID and Password. Post successful authentication, click on “Access to 
e-Voting”
 IV.  Click on company name i.e. ‘Thermax Limited’ or e-Voting service provider i.e. KFintech and you 
will be re-directed to e-Voting service provider website for casting the vote during the remote 
e-Voting period.
2. Member not registered for IDeAS e-Services
 I. To register click on link : https://eservices.nsdl.com

IdeasDirectReg.jsp
 III. Proceed with completing the required fields.
 IV. Follow steps given in points 1.
3. Alternatively, by directly accessing the e-Voting website of NSDL
 I. Open URL: https://www.evoting.nsdl.com/
 II. Click on the icon “Login” which is available under ‘Shareholder/Member’ section.
 III.  A new screen will open. Members will have to enter their User ID (i.e. their sixteen digit demat 
account number held with NSDL), Password/OTP and a Verification Code as shown on the screen.
 IV.  Post successful authentication, Members will be requested to select the name of the company and 
the e-Voting Service Provider name, i.e. KFintech.
 V.  On successful selection, Members will be redirected to KFintech e-Voting page for casting your 
vote during the remote e-Voting period.

Business with a PurposeType of Member Login Method
 iv.  Members will now reach the password change Menu wherein they are required to mandatorily 
change the password. The new password shall comprise of minimum 8 characters with at least 
one upper case (A-Z), one lower case (a-z), one numeric value (0-9) and a special character 
(@,#,$, etc.,). The system will prompt the members to change their password and update their 
contact details viz. mobile number, email ID etc. on first login. Members may also enter a secret 
question and answer of their choice to retrieve their password in case they forget it. It is strongly 
recommended that members do not share their password with any other person and that they take 
utmost care to keep their password confidential.
 v. Members would need to login again with the new credentials.
 vi.  On successful login, the system will prompt the member to select the “EVEN”, viz., ‘Thermax 
Limited 9820’, and click on “Submit”.
 vii.  On the voting page, enter the number of shares (which represents the number of votes) as on the 
Cut-off Date under “FOR/AGAINST” or alternatively, a member may partially enter any number in 
“FOR” and partially “AGAINST” but the total number in “FOR/AGAINST” taken together shall not 
exceed the total shareholding as mentioned herein above. A member may also choose the option 
ABSTAIN. If a member does not indicate either “FOR” or “AGAINST” it will be treated as “ABSTAIN” 
and the shares held will not be counted under either head.
 viii.  Members holding multiple folios/demat accounts shall choose the voting process separately for 
each folio/demat account. Voting has to be done for each item of the notice separately. In case 
you do not desire to cast your vote on any specific item, it will be treated as abstained.
 ix.  Members may then cast their vote by selecting an appropriate option and click on “Submit”.
 x.  A confirmation box will be displayed. Click “OK” to confirm else “CANCEL” to modify. Once 
members have voted on the resolution(s), they will not be allowed to modify their vote. During the 
voting period, members can login any number of times till they have voted on the Resolution.
 xi.  Corporate/Institutional members (corporate/FIs/FIIs/trust/mutual funds/banks, etc.) are required 
to send scanned certified true copy (pdf format) of the relevant board resolution/authority letter 
etc., authorising its representative to attend the AGM through VC/OAVM on its behalf and cast 
its vote through remote e-voting with attested specimen signature(s) of the duly authorised 
representative(s), to the Scrutinizer through e-mail to cs@svdandassociates.com with a copy to 
evoting@kfintech.com The file scanned image/pdf file of the board resolution should be in the 
naming format “Corporate Name_Even No”. In case if remote e-voting, the said documents should 
reach the Scrutinizer on/or before Wednesday, July 29, 2026 at 5.00 p.m. IST.

commencement of the Meeting.

through Laptops/Desktops with Google Chrome 
(preferred browser), Safari, Internet Explorer, 
Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox 22.

the webcam to enable VC/OAVM. Further,

Hotspot may experience Audio/Video loss due  
to fluctuation in their respective network.  
It is therefore recommended to use stable  
Wi-Fi or LAN Connection to mitigate any kind

OAVM, for the smooth conduct of proceedings

through e-Voting system available during the AGM. E-voting during the AGM is integrated with

on the voting icon displayed on the screen to cast 
their votes.
 vii.  A Member can opt for only single mode of voting 
i.e., through Remote e-voting or voting at the 
AGM. If a Member cast votes by both modes, then 
voting done through Remote e-voting shall prevail 
and vote at the AGM shall be treated as invalid.
 viii.  Facility of joining the AGM through VC/OAVM 
shall be available for at least 2000 members on 
first come first served basis. The said restrictions

11.  The dividend income is taxable in the hands of 
shareholders and the Company is required to deduct 
tax at source from dividend paid to shareholders at the 
prescribed rates. For the prescribed rates for various 
categories, the shareholders are requested to refer 
to the Income Tax Act, 2025. The shareholders are 
requested to update their PAN with the Company/
KFintech (in case of shares held in physical mode) and 
depositories (in case of shares held in demat mode). 
The applicable rate depends on the shareholder’s 
residential status, availability of valid PAN, tax treaty 
benefits (in case of non-resident shareholders) & 
special exemptions, if any, and submission of all 
requisite details & documents to the Company.

16. National Electronic Clearing Service (NECS):
  The Company has provided facility to the Members for 
receiving dividend through Electronic Clearing System 
(ECS) to avoid loss in transit/fraudulent interception 
& encashment/undue delay in receipt of the dividend 
warrant. The ECS facility is available at locations 
approved by the Reserve Bank of India from time to 
time and covers most of the cities and towns.
  Members holding shares in physical form and who 
wish to avail this facility are requested to send their 
details in the ECS mandate form. The ECS mandate 
form may be collected from the Company’s Corporate 
Office or its Registrar & Transfer Agent (RTA) or may 
be downloaded from the Company’s website ( www.
thermaxglobal.com ). The ECS mandate form submitted 
earlier shall be valid for the recommended dividend.
  Members are requested to intimate changes, if 
any, pertaining to their name, postal address, email 
address, telephone/mobile numbers, Permanent 
Account Number (PAN), mandates, nominations, 
power of attorney, bank details such as, name of the 
bank and branch details, bank account number, MICR 
code, IFSC code, etc., to their DPs in case the shares 
are held by them in electronic form and to KFintech in 
case the shares are held by them in physical form.
17 . Unclaimed Dividend:
  The Ministry of Corporate Affairs had notified 
provisions relating to unpaid/unclaimed dividend 
under Sections 124 and 125 of the Companies Act, 
2013 and the Investor Education and Protection Fund 
(Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 
(IEPF Rules). As per these Rules, dividends which 
are not encashed/claimed by the shareholder for a 
period of seven consecutive years shall be transferred 
to the Investor Education and Protection Fund 
(IEPF) Authority.  The IEPF Rules mandate the companies to transfer 
such shares of Members of whom dividends remain 
unpaid/unclaimed for a period of seven consecutive 
years to the demat account of IEPF Authority.
  Dividend declared by the Company on August 8, 
2019 for the financial year 2018-19 which remained 
unclaimed, is due to transfer to the IEPF, on September 
10, 2026, pursuant to the provisions of the aforesaid 
Sections of the Companies Act, 2013.
  Members who have not encashed their dividend 
warrants pertaining to the year 2018-19 and/or any 
subsequent years that still remains outstanding, 
are requested to lodge their claims with KFintech, 
the Company’s RTA, at the earliest for obtaining 
payments thereof.
18. Queries related to Financial Statements:
  Members are requested to write to the Company their 
queries, if any, on the financial statements, at least 10 
days before the meeting to enable the management to 
keep the required information available.
  The audited financial statements and consolidated 
financial statements for the financial year ended March

  The SEBI has established a common Online Dispute

Item No. 5
The Members of the Company, at the 41st Annual General 
Meeting held on August 2, 2022, had approved the 
appointment of Dr. Ravi Shankar Gopinath (DIN: 00803847) 
as the Non-Executive, Independent Director of the 
Company for a period of five consecutive years to hold the 
office up to November 9, 2026.
Section 149(10) of the Act provides that an Independent 
Director shall hold office for a term of five consecutive 
years on the Board of the Company but shall be eligible 
for re-appointment on passing of Special Resolution by 
the Company and disclosure of such appointment in the 
Board’s Report. Further, Section 149(11) provides that no 
Independent Director shall hold office for more than two 
consecutive terms. Dr. Gopinath has completed one term 
and is further eligible for re-appointment for a second term.
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) 
evaluated Dr. Gopinath’s skillset, knowledge, experience 
and noted the outcome of his annual performance 
evaluation during his tenure. The Committee also took note 
of Dr. Gopinath’s meaningful contributions to the Board 
and the Committees of which he is a member. The NRC 
acknowledged his consistent and committed participation 
in Board and Committee meetings throughout his tenure. The details pertaining to his membership on various 
committees of the Board are set forth in the Corporate 
Governance Report.
Accordingly, based on the above factors, the NRC 
recommended to the Board the re-appointment of 
Dr. Gopinath as Independent Director of the Company. The 
Board of Directors of the Company, at its Meeting held on 
May 7, 2026, approved the proposal for re-appointment 
of Dr. Gopinath as Non-Executive, Independent Director 
for a second term of five consecutive years commencing 
from November 10, 2026 till November 9, 2031 (both days 
inclusive), not liable to retire by rotation.
The Company has received a notice in writing under Section 
160(1) of the Act from a Member, proposing the candidature 
of Dr. Gopinath as an Independent Director of the Company.
The Company has also received the following from 
Dr. Gopinath:

Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014;

Group as Managing Director and CEO since September 
1 , 2020. Under his leadership, the Group has been 
steadfast in advancing its strategic direction to become 
a trusted partner in energy transition and sustainability. 
With a focus on driving innovation and creating long-term 
value, Ashish spearheads initiatives to maintain Thermax’s 
leadership in energy and environment solutions. He 
is instrumental in strengthening global customer and 
partner relationships, steering the Group’s expansion into 
emerging sectors and markets, and adapting to evolving 
business models and industry trends to ensure the Group 
remains agile and future-ready.
A passionate advocate for innovation, Ashish drives 
Thermax’s global product and service development 
strategies, ensuring they align with the changing needs 
of industries and the broader goal of decarbonisation. 
Ashish has been at the forefront of Thermax’s digital 
transformation journey, leveraging cutting-edge 
technologies such as AI, IIoT, and data analytics to 
enhance product offerings and operational efficiency. 
His commitment to innovation is reshaping how 
Thermax delivers value to customers in an increasingly 
technology-driven world. He envisions that by 2030, a 
significant portion of Thermax’s portfolio will comprise 
businesses that are currently in nascent stages, reflecting 
his commitment to fostering growth in new areas.
Ashish brings over two decades of rich and diverse 
experience from world-leading organisations across 
industries. Before joining Thermax, he served as Vice 
President for India and South Asia regions at Baker 
Hughes (formerly a GE company), where he played 
a pivotal role in driving growth across the region. His 
15-year tenure at GE included several senior leadership 
roles, building expertise in operational excellence and 
market expansion. Earlier in his career, he contributed to 
leading organisations such as Schlumberger, McKinsey 
& Company, and two international startups, giving him a 
unique perspective on global business dynamics.
Ashish holds a Bachelor of Technology (B. Tech) in 
Electrical Engineering from the prestigious Indian 
Institute of Technology, Bombay, and an MBA from 
Duke University. His educational foundation, combined 
with his extensive professional experience, underpins 
his strategic leadership at Thermax.Dr. Gopinath is the Chief Strategy Officer at AVEVA plc, 
a FTSE listed software company. He joined AVEVA in 
20 18 through the merger of Schneider Electric Software 
with AVEVA. Prior to the merger, he was the Executive 
Vice President of Schneider Electric Software. He joined 
Schneider Electric in 20 14 following the acquisition 
of Invensys plc by Schneider Electric, where he was 
President of Invensys Software.
He started his career as a research scientist in Tata 
Consultancy Services in 1994 and eventually led the 
global Engineering Business and the Manufacturing 
Practice for the company. He left TCS in 2006 and 
joined Geometric Ltd. as the MD and CEO. He held that

01 Thermax Limited  �  Annual Report 2025-26
Our ethos of being a ‘business with a 
purpose’ dates back to our beginnings as 
a small boiler manufacturer. As Thermax 
marks 60 years, this belief stands 
reaffirmed, guiding not only what we do, 
but how we do it.
Over the decades, as we have evolved into a global energy 
and environment solutions company, our conviction has 
remained constant: business can, and must, be a force 
for good.
Today, this philosophy shapes how we serve industries 
across the world. Through our integrated portfolio, we enable 
customers to meet their energy and resource needs while 
advancing environmental responsibility, delivering clean air, 
clean energy and clean water. Innovation remains central 
to this journey. From biofuels, green hydrogen and carbon 
capture to advanced water and wastewater solutions and 
digital enablement, we are helping industries grow while 
transitioning towards more sustainable pathways.
This progress is anchored in the trust of our customers, the 
support of our partners and suppliers, and the commitment 
of our people. Together, we are building an ecosystem 
rooted in responsible practices, collaboration and shared 
value creation.
Beyond business, we remain committed to creating a 
broader societal impact. Through our CSR initiatives, we 
focus on education, skill development and community 
well-being, ensuring that the benefits of our work extend far 
beyond our operations.
As we celebrate this milestone year, we look ahead with both 
gratitude and resolve. Thermax at 60 is not just a reflection of 
our journey so far, but a renewed commitment to shaping a 
more purposeful and sustainable future, for industry, society 
and the planet.

GroupsPlanetAbout this Integrated Report
We are pleased to present the Integrated Report for 
FY 2025-26, outlining how Thermax Limited (Thermax) and 
its group of companies create value for stakeholders in 
the short, medium, and long term. The report provides a 
comprehensive overview of our financial and non-financial 
performance, strategic priorities, governance framework, 
operating context and the key risks and opportunities 
shaping our future. 
In line with SEBI regulations, we also publish our Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) for Thermax 
Limited, which details our stakeholder-relevant performance. 
To enhance clarity and avoid duplication, we have combined 
the Integrated Report and the BRSR into a single, cohesive 
document that delivers a balanced and concise perspective 
for all our stakeholders. 
Throughout this report, the terms ‘Thermax,’ ‘Thermax 
Group,’ ‘the Group,’ ‘the Company,’ ‘your Company,’ 
‘we,’ ‘our,’ and ‘us’ refer to Thermax Limited and/or our 
Group companies.
Framework, Guidelines and Standards
This Report has been developed in alignment with the 
Integrated Reporting (<IR>) framework issued by the 
International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) 
Foundation, a global non-for-profit organisation, which 
promotes high-quality, globally accepted standards for 
financial and sustainability reporting. The non-financial 
disclosures contained herein are prepared with reference to 
the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards 2021.

accounting requirements:

Understanding Thermax
Headquartered in Pune, Thermax Limited (NSE: THERMAX) 
has been at the forefront of the energy and environment 
sector since 1966. As a trusted partner in the global energy 
transition, we deliver sustainable solutions to industries 
across heating, cooling, power generation, and air 
pollution control.
Our expertise in water and wastewater treatment and 
recycling enables customers to optimise resource 
efficiency, while our range of chemicals is engineered to 
deliver high performance across diverse applications.
Driven by our commitment to clean air, clean energy, and 
clean water, we provide integrated, future-ready solutions 
supported by strategic partnerships and a strong culture 
of innovation.16

Key Highlights of FY 2025-26   
Financials Thermax recorded a consolidated revenue of Rs. 10,694 crore in FY 2025-26, up 3.1% as 
compared to Rs. 10,369 crore in FY 2024-25. Consolidated PAT stood at Rs. 720 crore, up 14.9% 
from  Rs. 627 crore in the previous year. Order booking grew 34.2% to Rs. 13,871 crore, compared 
to Rs. 10,337 crore in FY 2024-25.
30 Years of Listing 
on the National 
Stock ExchangeIn 2025, Thermax marked 30 years since its listing on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) with 
a ceremonial bell-ringing event in Mumbai. Hosted by the NSE, the occasion was attended 
by members of the promoter family, the Managing Director & CEO, former and current Board 
members, senior leaders, customers, and long-standing stakeholders who have contributed  
to the Company’s growth and evolution over the past three decades.
Major Project  
WinThermax Babcock & Wilcox Energy Solutions Limited (TBWES) secured a breakthrough boiler 
package supply order valued at approximately Rs. 1,600 crore from a leading thermal power 
projects company in Central India for a 1 x 800 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power plant.

Value CreationMESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRPERSON
A Legacy of Purpose,  
A Future of PossibilitiesMy Dear Shareholders,
Sixty Years of Building with Purpose
The year under review holds special significance for all 
of us at Thermax. In 2026, we complete 60 years as an 
institution shaped by purpose, resilience, passion and the 
collective efforts of generations of Thermaxians and all our 
stakeholders. More than a milestone of longevity, it is an 
opportunity to reflect on the values that have guided us since 
the beginning — integrity, respect, responsible growth and 
creating value for every stakeholder.
This year also marked 30 years of Thermax's listing on the 
National Stock Exchange. The bell-ringing ceremony at the 
NSE was both nostalgic and humbling. It reminded me of 
my grandfather, Adi Bhathena, who laid the foundation of 
this institution; my father, Rohinton Aga, the visionary, who 
expanded and grew the portfolio and took the Company 
public in 1995; and my mother, Anu Aga, who steered 
Thermax through one of its most difficult phases with 
courage and conviction. It was also a reminder of the many 
people (both past and present) who have made this journey 
possible, with their passion  and trust — our customers 
who believe in us, giving us an opportunity to improve their 
business; our vendors who have partnered with us in building 
solutions; our channel partners who have grown with us, 
carrying the Thermax brand; our communities that ground 
us in purpose; our shareholders who have placed their 
confidence and trust in us and our Board members, whose 
wisdom has guided us over the years.
Thank you all from the bottom of my heart.
Operating in a Changing Global Landscape
The year under review unfolded against a backdrop of 
considerable geopolitical uncertainty. Ongoing conflicts 
across regions, particularly in the Middle East, disrupted 
trade flows, impacted commodity prices and created 
volatility across logistics and global supply chains.  
These developments affected industries worldwide and had 
implications for some of Thermax's businesses, especially 
those dependent on international sourcing and exports to the 
Middle East.
At the same time, these uncertainties have reinforced an 
important reality. For India, ‘energy security’ has moved 
beyond economic necessity, to become a strategic 
imperative. The real challenge is to achieve energy 
security while accelerating energy transition and meeting 
decarbonisation goals. This is where Thermax believes it can 
create the most meaningful impact.
Amidst global uncertainty, India's economic trajectory 
remained a source of confidence. Real GDP growth held 
at approximately 7 .6%, supported by the government's continued commitment to infrastructure investment, clean 
energy acceleration and industrial decarbonisation. Policy 
frameworks around bioenergy adoption, green hydrogen 
mobilisation, emission reduction norms and energy-efficient 
manufacturing continue to create direct and specific demand 
for energy and environmental solutions.
Business Performance and Strategic 
Progress
Despite the challenging global environment, the year was 
marked by steady progress across several areas of our 
business. We maintained healthy order inflows and built 
a robust order backlog of Rs. 13,604 crore with a marked 
improvement in the quality of orders. Although revenue 
growth was subdued at Rs. 10,694 crore, our profit after 
tax grew substantially to Rs. 720 crore. The Board has 
recommended a total dividend of Rs. 20 per equity share, 
which includes a one-time special dividend of Rs. 6 per 
share, to mark the Company's 60th anniversary.
Our Industrial Products business continued to build 
strong momentum through innovative solutions in process 
heating, water and wastewater and air pollution control. 
Our engineering legacy of six decades gives us a deep 
understanding of industrial process realities. Products that 
enhance efficiency using AI-based controllers for boilers 
and heaters, are the natural evolution of that institutional 
knowledge, combining decades of application expertise 
with the possibilities of modern data science. Across our 
businesses, our EDGE Live platform monitors a number of 
customer assets across geographies, creating value for our 
customers through digital innovation.Amidst global uncertainty, India's 
economic trajectory remained a 
source of confidence. Real GDP 
growth held at approximately 7 .6%, 
supported by the government's 
continued commitment to 
infrastructure investment, clean 
energy acceleration and industrial 
decarbonisation. Policy frameworks 
around bioenergy adoption, green 
hydrogen mobilisation, emission 
reduction norms and energy-efficient 
manufacturing continue to create 
direct and specific demand for energy 
and environmental solutions.We maintained healthy  
order inflows and built a 
robust order backlog of  
Rs. 13,604 crore with a 
marked improvement in the 
quality of orders.

Value Creation
The Water and Waste Solutions (WWS) business 
strengthened its position through new-age solutions in 
desalination, water recycling, zero liquid discharge and 
brine recovery, reflecting our focus on sustainable water 
management and the circular economy.
The entry of Cooling & Heating business into the US and 
India data centre markets, driven by the explosion in AI 
infrastructure demand, opens a new growth frontier. 
Our Air Pollution Control business also continued to 
strengthen its presence with multiple installations across 
international markets.
Industrial Infra received a landmark boiler package supply 
order of approximately Rs. 1,600 crore for a 1 × 800 MW 
ultra-supercritical thermal power plant in Central India, 
reinforcing the engineering credentials of the Company 
at the highest levels of complexity. We are also looking to 
establish India's first green methanol facility at Deendayal 
Port, Kandla, Gujarat, turning agricultural waste and local 
biomass into cleaner shipping fuels.
Part of our Green Solutions portfolio continued to strengthen 
during the year with TOESL (utilities on hire) leading the 
way. This vertical also forged through strategic partnerships 
and new initiatives that directly address India's energy 
challenges. Our recent collaboration with Norway-based 
HydrogenPro ASA enables us to offer market-ready alkaline 
electrolyser solutions in India.
Chemicals faced significant headwinds during the year — 
geopolitical disruptions, volatility in raw material prices, 
a constrained demand that has only recently begun to 
recover, and higher costs due to low capacity utilisation at 
a new plant. The Fortmax brand, born from our alliance with 
Oswaldo Cruz Química (OCQ), represents a move to high-
performance speciality chemicals, where production has 
just commenced.
Navigating Challenges with Discipline
Amongst our Green Solutions vertical, First Energy Private 
Limited (FEPL) – a 100% subsidiary providing green power 
on solar and wind projects to the commercial and industrial 
segment, has not been performing as planned. Alongside the 
external environment, we continued to navigate operational 
complexities and execution challenges. The Company is 
implementing corrective measures to strengthen execution 
and improve delivery timelines. Thermax Bioenergy Solutions 
Private Limited (TBSPL), our bio-CNG business is in the 
process of commissioning and handing over plants across 
India. Although challenging, we have had significant learnings 
that can be applied to new orders going forward.60 years of building an institution also means 60 years of 
accountability and responsibility, to every life entrusted to 
Thermax's care. Despite having strong safety systems and 
processes in place, we experienced four fatalities during 
the year — a matter of deep concern for all of us. The Board 
has discussed a fundamental reassessment of our safety 
governance structure at the leadership level, apart from 
continuous safety training and ensuring safety is embedded 
in our engineering.
Empowering People, Building the Future
At the heart of any enduring institution are its people and the 
culture they help shape every day. This year, we continued 
to invest in building our leadership pipeline through various 
leadership development programmes for our executives, 
senior and young leaders, building an internal pipeline. In 
order to listen more deeply, understand what matters to 
our employees, and act in a more structured manner, we 
have pivoted to an annual employee survey. Our focus on 
employee well-being through mental health support, learning 
opportunities and a culture of open dialogue, reflects 
our belief that people who feel valued and heard, are the 
foundation of everything we build. We remain encouraged 
by the commitment and positive energy we see across the 
organisation and are deeply grateful for it.
On behalf of our Board, I am pleased to welcome 
Kavita Singh to our Executive Council as Chief Human 
Resources Officer and look forward to her leadership 
in further strengthening our people practices and 
organisational culture.
Creating Impact Beyond Business
Anu has long believed that “business cannot succeed in a 
society that fails”. At Thermax Foundation, we have carved 
our work into three verticals: education and skilling (being 
the largest), agriculture and farming and animal welfare. 
We strengthened our educational outreach through project 
SETU with the Akanksha Foundation, scaling effective 
teaching-learning practices across Pimpri Chinchwad, Pune 
and Nagpur. We supported 1,484 young people through 
industry-aligned ITI programmes, each gaining the dignity of 
skilled work and a pathway to self-reliance.
Through the NGO Manavlok, we enabled 409 small farmers 
to adopt scientific practices and access export markets. 
We also embarked on something more ambitious — 
restoring agricultural land with energy crops across 500 
acres, conceived by our late Board member Dr. Ravi Pandit with a clear and meaningful purpose. Through watershed 
development and sustainable biomass cultivation, we are 
creating community-led bioenergy value chains, while laying 
the foundation for biomass-to-green hydrogen opportunities, 
embodying our conviction that ecological restoration and 
rural prosperity are at the heart of energy transition.
Through our work in ‘Social Compact’, we continue to 
facilitate access to government schemes and social security 
for the unorganised sector.
Looking ahead, we also intend to extend our community work 
to animal welfare with a focus on reducing human-animal 
conflicts and fostering peaceful coexistence in Pune, to 
begin with.
This year, over 650 Thermaxians volunteered across 
these programmes, bringing genuine human connection 
and mentorship.Looking Ahead with Purpose and 
Confidence
At this year's Board retreat, we spent considerable time 
discussing how Thermax can move closer to its vision of 
becoming ‘globally respected’, through simpler processes, 
stronger and safer execution, higher quality standards, 
greater investment in R&D, internationalisation, deeper 
customer partnerships and development of our people.
As we enter our 60th year, I find myself often thinking about 
what has made this organisation endure. What is truly distinct 
about this institution called Thermax? It is not our products, 
technologies or factories – it is our people.
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to our MD and 
CEO Ashish Bhandari, our leadership team, Board members, 
and every Thermaxian, for your unwavering motivation and 
dedication. My thanks to our customers, vendors, business 
and channel partners, shareholders, and communities for 
the trust and support that make ‘Thermax’ possible. It is this 
collective commitment that gives me confidence as we look 
to the future.
I look forward to continuing this journey together with 
renewed purpose, responsibility and confidence.
Warmly,
Meher Pudumjee

Building Thermax for the  
Next 30 YearsDear Stakeholders,
A Milestone and a Beginning
Last December, I had the privilege of joining several past 
and present Thermaxians at the National Stock Exchange 
to commemorate 30 years of Thermax’s listing. As we rang 
the ceremonial bell, it was natural to reflect on the journey 
that brought us here. The occasion recognised the fortitude 
of Mr. A. S. Bhathena and Mr. Rohinton Aga, the values and 
culture nurtured by Anu and Meher, and the contribution 
of generations of employees who have built Thermax over 
six decades.
A bell, however, does not only mark a celebration. It also 
symbolises the starting gun for the path ahead.
This year, Thermax completes 60 years. Our history gives us 
a strong foundation to build a company that can thrive in this 
world of change. Energy security has once again become 
a strategic priority for nations. Climate change, water 
scarcity and deteriorating air quality are becoming more 
urgent. Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries while 
creating unprecedented demand for power, cooling and 
infrastructure. India must grow rapidly while reducing  
the resource and environmental intensity of that growth.
These shifts make Thermax more relevant than ever.
Momentum Returned, but More Was 
Possible
FY26 was a good year in many ways. Orders grew from  
Rs. 10,337 crore to Rs. 13,871 crore, resulting in a healthy 
order backlog of Rs. 13,604 crore, up 27.2% year-on-year, 
which will be carried forward to FY27. More importantly, 
the quality of orders improved and along the lines of our 
commitments, we did not undertake large project orders with 
long gestation and significant civil and construction scope. 
International business revenue also continued to grow, 
reaching Rs. 3,084 crore, up 33.4% in FY26.
Our Industrial Infra business secured important orders 
in India and overseas. These included utility boilers for a 
refinery project in Nigeria, boilers for a strategic Middle 
East oil & gas customer, and a supercritical boiler project in 
India. The business also improved profitability despite lower 
revenue, supported by a better project mix and improved 
execution. The supercritical project has been undertaken 
with careful thought and due resource allocation. 
We also made progress in bio-CNG. All 14 plants have now 
been commissioned. Collectively, these plants produced 19,400 tonnes of compressed biogas during the year 
and crossed production of 100 tonnes per day in January 
2026. The journey has not been easy, and plant availability 
remains an area of focus, but valuable lessons are being 
translated into operational improvements. The order for 
India’s first 5 TPD green methanol facility at Kandla Port, 
Gujarat, is an important example of research moving towards 
commercial application.
Industrial Products delivered broad-based growth. Our 
Cooling business secured its first large data centre orders in 
both India and the United States. Water and Waste Solutions, 
Air Pollution Control and Process Heat Solutions also 
recorded growth across domestic and international markets.
Several initiatives that were small or did not exist three years 
ago are now becoming meaningful businesses. These 
include zero liquid discharge, waste-to-energy, heat pumps, 
hybrid CLCTs (closed-loop cooling towers), gas purification & 
upgradation, urban water solutions, electric boilers, Thermax 
EDGE Live® (IIoT), and lifecycle services.
In Green Solutions, TOESL continued to perform strongly 
while expanding internationally. We now operate over 47 
plants and source more than 3,500 tonnes of biomass 
daily, making us one of India's largest organised biomass 
aggregators. Our Green Hydrogen team is making good 
progress towards a solid oxide electrolyser demonstration 
plant, while our partnership with HydrogenPro enables us to 
offer competitive alkaline electrolyser solutions today.
Our renewable energy business (FEPL) continued to 
scale, with the total capacity of solar, wind, and wind-solar 
hybrid projects under open access reaching 235.5 MWp to 
date. During the year, the growth in revenue was modest, 
especially given the investments made and the opportunities 
available to us. Project delays and operational challenges 
persist, and addressing these remains a clear priority for the 
team for the year ahead. 
Our Cooling business 
secured its first large data 
centre orders in both India 
and the United States.

Value CreationMESSAGE FROM THE MD & CEO
In Chemicals, the new resin plant in Jhagadia, Gujarat, has 
rapidly stabilised. There is progress in our partnerships, 
Vebro Polymers and OCQ, albeit below our original plans. 
International growth was also below plan but there were 
good breakthroughs towards the end of the year. The Ion 
Exchange Resin business expanded into new application 
areas, including PFAS removal for water treatment and 
speciality additives for ceramics, creating avenues for 
future growth.
There were areas where we could have done better.  
Revenue and profits were both short of targets as we 
started the year slow and heavy monsoons impeded project 
progress for several months. Most projects progressed 
broadly in line with expectations during the year. However, 
one large and complex project that was undertaken in FY22 
experienced delays arising from design changes, vendor-
related disruptions and site execution challenges. Progress 
at certain bio-CNG sites was also slower than planned, 
impacting the pace of revenue growth.
Safety is another area where we need to do better. In our 
efforts to strengthen the safety culture, we undertook  
several key initiatives under the Behaviour Based Safety 
(BBS) Programme, with structured implementation across  
all our plants. 
As we enter FY 2026-27, our order backlog provides 
confidence, but rising commodity prices, weather-related 
uncertainties, and the impact of the Gulf War on energy 
prices and global supply chains continue to demand the 
utmost attention to business operations.
Energy Security and Energy Sustainability
In recent years, the discussion at Thermax has centred 
more on energy transition. Events of the past year have 
again highlighted the importance of energy security. 
Nations and companies need access to energy that is 
reliable and affordable. At the same time, the environmental 
consequences of how that energy is produced and 
consumed cannot be ignored.
Energy security and energy sustainability must therefore 
progress together. As an example, in India, thermal power 
is once again on the discussion table with several projects, 
subcritical and supercritical, being conceptualised by our 
customers. Similarly, the bio-CNG policy is expected to be 
revised shortly, creating a fillip to this sector with significant green energy aspirations. Thermax’s role is to be the bridge 
between energy availability and energy sustainability. 
We must provide solutions that work technically and are 
commercially viable, while also reducing the environmental 
impact of growth.
The rise of artificial intelligence and data centres is one 
example. Data centres require large quantities of reliable 
power and efficient cooling. Thermax can participate across 
this value chain through power and heat recovery systems, 
absorption cooling, water treatment solutions and digital 
optimisation. Our recent data centre orders in India and the 
United States are early steps in developing this opportunity.
India’s challenge is larger, though. The country needs to 
expand manufacturing, infrastructure and energy supply 
while also addressing pollution, water stress and carbon 
intensity. Renewable electricity is important, but it is only one 
part of the answer. Industrial heat, energy efficiency, water 
reuse, clean air, bioenergy, green chemicals and resource 
conservation will be equally relevant.
Building Thermax for the Next 30 Years
Thermax’s growth has mirrored that of India. From a fledgling 
company that went through highs and lows, we have now 
emerged with capabilities and strength across sectors and 
geographies. To build a Thermax for the next 30 years is 
to build a company that is relevant to the challenges of the 
coming times and also one that can compete with and be the 
best globally.
Building and commercialising new technologies and 
continuous innovation is one key aspect of achieving this 
vision, but that by itself is not enough.
Thermax’s execution and quality must be world-class. 
The customer experience we currently provide is varied, 
especially when it comes to site execution and project 
management. Total System Quality (TSQ) includes a 
comprehensive look at the quality of our offering in a 
way that encompasses engineering, sourcing, vendors, 
manufacturing, construction, commissioning, project 
management and service. TSQ is a multi-year journey 
targeting global benchmarks on quality and speed. TSQ  
is a key aspect of Thermax’s planned transformation.
The third is internationalisation. FY 2025-26 provided 
encouraging proof points across the world, including in 
the United States, the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia. International business now accounts for 29% of our 
sales. We will invest more in building capability to support 
customers locally. This means executing through local legal 
entities, hiring and training locally, and investing locally in 
service support.
The fourth is deeper customer partnerships. To be a 
trusted partner in energy transition, Thermax’s customer 
engagement model must be more integrated. Our Key 
Account Management (KAM) programme is being rolled 
out to understand customers’ longer-term priorities and 
work with them on solutions. Lifecycle services will be an 
important part of these relationships. Our installed base 
gives us the opportunity to support customers through 
operations and maintenance, upgrades, retrofits and 
performance improvement. Thermax EDGE Live®, our digital 
arm, can strengthen this further by helping customers 
improve operating performance.
Finally, growing functional expertise on the people 
front. Building new competencies requires enhanced 
functional capabilities in multiple areas, including digital, 
manufacturing, quality, sourcing, and civil and construction. 
We will develop this expertise through a deliberate mix of 
targeted training and experienced external hiring. 
Closing
In May this year, the world lost Dr. Ravi Pandit, a member 
of the Thermax Board and a leading light of India. Ravi 
consistently encouraged Thermax to invest more in R&D 
and to take on the difficult energy transition problems facing the country. He practised what he preached. His work 
in hydrogen fuel cells, sodium ion batteries and biofuels 
reflected a willingness to invest in technologies well before 
their commercial potential was clear. Thermax’s current R&D 
programme is influenced by his thinking and encouragement.
I thank the Thermax Board for its guidance and trust. I thank 
our customers, partners, vendors and shareholders for their 
continued support. Most importantly, I thank my leadership 
team and Thermax employees across our offices, factories 
and project sites.
The NSE bell commemorated an important milestone in 
Thermax’s history. It also marked the beginning of the 
next phase—to build a Thermax that can thrive for the next 
30 years.
Best regards,
Ashish Bhandari
MD & CEO

Steering Confidently Amidst 
Uncertainties
At Thermax, we recognise that risks are inherent in a dynamic global environment. We proactively identify, assess, and mitigate 
potential challenges to protect our stakeholders and maintain peak performance. Our forward-thinking approach safeguards our 
operations and uncovers opportunities for continuous improvement, ensuring we remain resilient and agile in the face of change.
Thermax is exposed to multiple diverse risks in the current changing environment. The risk management framework in Thermax 
is integral to the Company’s functioning and facilitates timely assessment and mitigation of risks at enterprise and operational 
level. The risk management processes regularly apprise the Risk Management Committee about identified and potential risks.     
Definition:
• Loss of reputation/market share/
margin erosion due to inadequate 
process framework and monitoring of 
risks during the project lifecycle.
• Huge project delays (supply and 
construction) may result in higher 
costs, liquidated damages, reduction 
of margins and loss of reputation.
• Delays in delivery of key raw materials 
and equipment due to supplier issues, 
logistical bottlenecks may lead to cost 
escalations and adversely impact 
project execution.
• Health and safety risks from high-risk 
operations in projects and services. 
These include workplace accidents, 
equipment failures, steam exposure 
and fire. Any safety lapses may lead to 
injuries, operational disruptions, legal 
issues and reputational damage.
Definition:
• Inability to identify, classify, 
document, digitise and archive 
business-critical knowledge/
information to ensure complete, 
consistent, reliable, and secure 
corporate data.
• Adverse impact on the Company’s 
operations due to cyberattacks 
and lack of firewalls, encryption, 
and remote access controls, 
leading to compromise 
of confidential data and 
intellectual property. 
• Inability to continue/recover 
business operations during 
any crisis, and/or disaster, 
with minimal disruption or loss 
of business.Mitigation Plan:
• Continuous monitoring mechanism at all levels within the 
organisation with special focus on costs.
• Assessing and mitigating risks and ensuring timely execution of 
projects with the help of advanced project management tools 
deployed in the organisation.
• Developing strategic partnerships with suppliers and sub-
contractors to ensure timely supply of material.
• Thermax has implemented robust ISO 45001-aligned safety 
management systems, supported by regular risk assessments, 
SOP compliance, preventive maintenance, safe chemical 
handling, emergency preparedness, and real-time monitoring 
to minimise workplace risks. 
• Comprehensive training programmes, mandatory PPE 
(personal protective equipment) usage, and strong contractor 
safety protocols have been established.
• The Company continues to strengthen its Behaviour-Based 
Safety (BBS) journey, fostering an ownership-led safety culture 
through capability building, digital contractor competency 
management, and the Thermax LIFE HSE platform, which 
enables reporting, inspections, audits, action tracking, and 
real-time safety analytics.
Mitigation Plan:
• Thermax has established a comprehensive cybersecurity risk 
management framework across all business units to identify, 
assess, and manage cyber risks. The evolving threat landscape 
is continuously monitored through advanced cybersecurity 
monitoring and incident response mechanisms, with 
appropriate preventive and corrective controls implemented to 
mitigate identified risks.
• Robust disaster recovery and business continuity procedures 
are in place for all critical applications. These arrangements are 
periodically tested to validate their effectiveness and to ensure 
operational resilience and continuity of business operations in 
the event of system disruptions or cyber incidents. 
• The Business Technology Group (BTG) regularly apprises 
senior management and the Risk Management Committee of 
the Board on the prevailing cyber risk landscape, emerging 
threats, and the progress of strategic and long-term initiatives 
undertaken to strengthen application and system security. 
This ensures ongoing oversight and alignment of cybersecurity 
efforts with the Company’s overall risk management and 
governance framework.Project Execution Risk

Definition:
• Impact on business dynamics 
due to restrictions and increase in 
compliance with conventional energy.
• Thermax may face a multifaceted 
set of climate change risks that 
span physical hazards, regulatory 
restrictions, supply chain disruptions, 
and impact on reputation. The 
core business lines may be 
exposed to climate risk thereby 
creating vulnerability.
Definition:
Inability to attract talent and 
plan succession of people for 
key positions.
Definition:
Ongoing global conflicts, especially in 
the Middle East regions may disrupt 
project execution, inflate input and 
logistics costs, and constrain demand 
across the key international markets 
(especially MENA and export-driven 
regions), thereby impacting revenues 
and margins.Mitigation Plan:
Thermax has prepared a detailed mitigation plan to address 
the risks and apprises the Risk Management Committee on the 
action plans. The plan addresses the following areas:
• Development of products/acquiring new technology on 
renewable energy - shifting from fossils to greener fuels.
• Measures are taken at all production facilities and 
projects sites to manage climatic conditions which may 
impact production work, project execution, equipment 
and workforce. 
Mitigation Plan:
• The Human Resources function has developed a robust 
leadership framework model which develops people 
who can lead in current business scenario aligned with 
company’s future vision & strategy. These leadership 
programmes are designed to develop successors at all 
levels to succeed people at all key positions.  
• To retain talent, the Function ensures career 
development, internal mobility programmes and skill-gap 
based coaching.
• The risk of regrettable attrition is addressed by 
strengthening manager–employee engagement, 
development plans for high-potential talent, systematic 
analysis of exit interviews and development of action plans 
to address structural issues.
Mitigation Plan:
• Diversify markets and supply chains across geographies 
(Asia, Africa, Europe) and adopt multi-sourcing to reduce 
dependence on high-risk regions like the Middle East and 
manage tariff and disruption exposure. 
• Strengthen project and supply chain resilience through 
scenario planning, real-time monitoring, flexible logistics, 
and contract/pricing adjustments to absorb cost shocks 
from tariffs, freight volatility, and energy price spikes. 
• Enhance risk governance and financial protection by 
implementing geopolitical risk tracking at leadership level, 
using insurance (political/war risk), hedging strategies, and 
localised execution models to ensure business continuity in 
volatile regions.

At Thermax, we integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) 
principles into our core strategy. This creates sustainable value for all 
stakeholders—investors, customers, employees, partners, communities 
and regulators, while safeguarding the planet. Our holistic approach 
drives innovation in clean technologies, fosters an inclusive workplace, 
and strengthens ethical governance. It also builds resilient supply chains. 
These efforts improve operational efficiency, enhance stakeholder trust and 
support long-term value creation. 
We align our decisions with global ESG standards and evolving stakeholder 
expectations. By doing so, we mitigate risks and unlock new opportunities, 
reinforcing Thermax’s resilience and positive impact over time.Vendors and

Build Your Own System: Gamifying the Way Water 
Solutions are Designed
Our Water and Waste Solutions (WWS) business has introduced 
Build Your Own System. This interactive platform enables 
customers to design customised water and wastewater 
treatment solutions for industrial and urban applications. It 
addresses emerging and next-generation challenges. The 
platform allows users to select appropriate technologies based 
on specific water quality requirements, operating conditions, 
and intended reuse or discharge standards. This enables more 
informed and efficient decision making.
Thermax's Water and Waste Solutions team along with customers at IFAT 2025SteamAssist: Powering Smart Decisions, 
Anytime, Anywhere
The Steam Engineering business has introduced 
SteamAssist, a mobile-based Knowledge Management 
System (KMS). It is designed to enhance productivity, 
collaboration and access to knowledge across teams. 
Developed for our Steam Sales and Service teams and 
Thermax Channel Associates (TCAs), the platform brings 
together training, engagement, marketing and sales 
resources into a single, user-friendly interface. This enables 
access anytime, anywhere. Features include on-the-go 
learning modules, interactive quizzes, real-time notifications 
and easy access to sales and marketing collaterals. 
SteamAssist supports continuous learning and informed 
decision making. A key highlight is the integration of savings 
calculators and industrial piping and instrumentation 
diagrams for steam and condensate systems. These 
offer practical, data-driven insights for field applications. 
This initiative represents a significant step in our digital 
transformation journey. It reinforces our commitment  
to empowering teams and delivering enhanced value  
to our customers.

Events and Exhibitions
Boiler World — Bangkok, Thailand
We participated in the Boiler World Expo S.E.A. 2025 in 
Bangkok through Thermax (Thailand) Ltd., marking our fifth 
consecutive year at the event. In alignment with Thailand 4.0, 
we showcased our integrated portfolio across clean air, clean 
energy, clean water, performance-engineered chemicals 
and digital solutions. Our exhibits included emission control 
technologies such as electrostatic precipitators and 
scrubbers, fuel-flexible and biomass-ready boilers, water 
and wastewater solutions including RO and ZLD, cooling 
systems, waste-to-energy capabilities and digital platforms 
such as Ultramind and Thermax EDGE Live®. Through 
customer engagements, seminars and panel discussions, we 
reinforced our role in supporting energy transition, industrial 
efficiency and sustainable growth across Thailand and 
Southeast Asia.
Thermax's booth at Boiler World S.E.A. that took 
place in Bangkok, ThailandAnnual Indonesia Green Industry Summit — 
Jakarta, Indonesia
We participated in the Annual Indonesia Green Industry 
Summit (AIGIS) through PT Thermax International Indonesia, 
engaging with government representatives, industry leaders 
and technology partners in support of Indonesia’s Net Zero 
Emissions 2060 vision. Our booth facilitated discussions 
with representatives from the Ministry of Industry on 
sustainable technologies and energy-efficient practices. 
We showcased solutions including high-efficiency boilers, 
biomass and alternative fuel systems, waste heat recovery, 
air pollution control, water and wastewater treatment, 
and decarbonisation services. These solutions cater to 
diverse industries, including F&B, textiles, chemicals, 
pharmaceuticals and palm oil. Through this platform, we 
reaffirmed our commitment to advancing Indonesia’s green 
industrial transformation.
IFAT India  — Mumbai, India
At IFAT India 2025, we unveiled one of our most 
comprehensive portfolios, spanning water, energy and 
environmental solutions. We highlighted a wide range 
of advanced solutions across digital monitoring, water 
and wastewater treatment, ZLD, and advanced filtration 
solutions. We also showcased innovations from across our 
businesses, including advanced combustion technologies, 
gas enrichment solutions, and our portfolio of chemicals 
and resins. Visitors participated in live demonstrations and 
previewed upcoming solutions, reinforcing our focus on 
future-ready technologies. Our pavilion also featured global 
partnerships with PureCODe, MUTAG Media, Atlantium, 
Symbiona and Primozone, demonstrating our ability to 
combine global expertise with local execution. The Build Your 
Own System (BYOS) Experience Zone enabled interactive 
engagement, illustrating our integrated approach to 
water and wastewater solutions. Overall, our participation 
reaffirmed our position as a trusted partner for sustainable 
industrial solutions.Gulfood Manufacturing — Dubai, United Arab 
Emirates
At Gulfood Manufacturing at the Dubai World Trade Centre, 
Thermax showcased its integrated energy and utility 
solutions tailored for the food and beverage industry. Our 
offerings spanned steam generation, process cooling, 
water and wastewater treatment, air pollution control, 
and speciality resins. Through interactions with regional 
stakeholders, we demonstrated how our solutions help 
enable efficient, reliable, and sustainable food processing 
operations, further strengthening our commitment to 
supporting the rapidly growing F&B sector in the Middle East.
TICE-EEA — Kuwait
At the 16th Technological Innovations Conference and 
Exposition (TICE) in Kuwait, Thermax presented a technical 
paper on energy transition and asset optimisation. The 
paper highlighted our service capabilities in enhancing asset 
reliability, operational efficiency and digital enablement 
through EDGE Live®. At the exhibition, we showcased our oil 
and gas solutions, attracting strong interest from industry 
stakeholders. A key highlight was the visit by the Chairman of 
Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC), during which 
we discussed opportunities to enhance existing assets with 
our solutions. Thermax Indonesia team at the AIGIS eventSTAKEHOLDER VALUE CREATION - CUSTOMERS

Customer Connect
Regional InTouch
As industries across India accelerate their transition 
towards sustainability, we continue to strengthen customer 
engagement through a series of regional connect 
programmes held in Kochi, Keralam; Visakhapatnam, 
Andhra Pradesh; Surat, Gujarat; and Ludhiana, Punjab. Each 
interaction serves as a platform for dialogue, collaboration 
and a shared commitment to advancing clean energy, air and 
water solutions.
In Kochi, the focus was on the plywood industry, with 
discussions centred around efficient heating and steam 
solutions under the theme ‘Trusted Partner in Energy 
Transition’. In Surat, engagements were tailored to the 
textile sector, highlighting sustainable process solutions for 
improved efficiency and reduced environmental impact.
Visakhapatnam brought together a diverse mix of industries 
including pharmaceuticals, chemicals, food processing and 
metals, where we showcased a wide range of technologies 
such as heat pumps, electric boilers, biomass-based utilities, 
water treatment and air pollution control systems.
In Ludhiana, conversations addressed region-specific 
challenges impacting industries such as agriculture-linked 
manufacturing and heavy engineering, including crop 
residue burning and industrial emissions. The discussions 
focused on solutions like biomass-based energy systems, 
flexible fuel technologies, bio-CNG initiatives and wastewater 
management, reinforcing our commitment to enabling 
sustainable industrial growth at a regional level.

EMPLOYEESCulture at Thermax
Rooted in Purpose, Driven by Impact
At Thermax, our culture is anchored in business with 
a purpose, where every action we take is aligned with 
creating long-term value for all our stakeholders. It goes 
beyond how we work, shaping how we engage with 
customers, partners, communities and each other. Built on 
a foundation of integrity, collaboration and accountability, 
our culture is brought to life through everyday actions and 
open communication.
We foster an environment where every voice matters. 
Through platforms like All Hands Meet and regular leadership 
updates, we encourage transparent, two-way dialogue that 
builds trust and alignment across the organisation. Our 
‘speak up’ approach empowers employees at all levels to 
share ideas, raise concerns and contribute meaningfully, 
reinforcing a culture of respect and inclusion.
As we continue to strengthen a performance-driven 
mindset, we remain focused on meaningful feedback, 
continuous learning and individual growth. While the journey 
is ongoing, our commitment is clear—to build a workplace 
where innovation thrives, diverse perspectives are valued, 
and every employee plays a vital role in shaping a more 
sustainable future.
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI)
Thermax is strongly committed to fostering a diverse and 
inclusive organisational culture, anchored in a clearly defined 
DEI strategy built around four core pillars. During the year, 
we implemented a range of initiatives aligned with these 
pillars to drive meaningful progress and cultivate an inclusive 
workplace environment.
1. Enhancing Gender Diversity 
At Thermax, our commitment to segmented hiring 
continues to support meaningful progress in building 
a gender-diverse workforce, particularly at the mid-
managerial level where future leadership is shaped. By 
consciously creating opportunities for women across 
business functions, we are strengthening our leadership 
pipeline for the long term. During the year, we increased 
women’s representation from 10.05% to 10.5%, reflecting 
an incremental progress in our diversity journey. This 
progress shows our commitment to advancing gender 
parity and fostering a workplace where all talent can grow 
and thrive.Leadership Conference

Employee Engagement – Annual Survey
In recent years, we have used Pulse surveys to gather 
employee feedback and understand their experience. 
We conduct these surveys multiple times a year to track 
engagement drivers and take prompt action. Building on 
these insights, we have now transitioned to a single Annual 
Survey format. This approach allows us to gain more 
comprehensive and meaningful insights across key themes, 
reduce survey fatigue and enable more structured and 
focused action planning.

Akanksha SETU Project
Initiated in 2022, the Akanksha SETU Project aims to scale 
Akanksha’s model of quality education across schools under 
the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) and 
Nagpur Municipal Corporation. Since then, it has evolved into 
an integrated intervention reaching 60,000 students across 
222 schools in both cities. Thermax Foundation has been 
supporting this project since 2025.
Key Highlights - Akanksha SETU Project
• Student enrolment in PCMC schools increased by 13%, 
from 48,153 to 54,418, alongside a 35% increase in the 
education budget, from Rs. 188 crore to Rs. 255 crore, 
reflecting strong government partnership and growing 
trust in the model. 
• One of the key highlights after Thermax's support to 
SETU has been fostering a partnership with Open 
Links app for large-scale assessments in PCMC. The 
Akanksha SETU Project targets on foundational literacy 
and numeracy (FLN) interventions. 
• Initiatives such as The Artbox in PCMC and Karnama in

Horti-Max FPO Project  
Near our Solapur factory in Maharashtra, we continued 
supporting Manavlok NGO through the Horti-Max Farmer 
Producer Organisation (FPO) Project, focused on building 
sustainable farming capabilities in water-deficient regions. 
The initiative supports around 409 small farmers through 
scientific and mechanised onion cultivation, supported by 
earlier watershed interventions.
During FY 2025–26, the project produced and sold 1,679 
tonnes of onions, generating over Rs. 2 crore in value. A 
total of 344 farmers earned approximately Rs. 3,660 more 
per farmer compared to traditional market sales. The FPO 
also exported 229 tonnes of onions valued at Rs. 45.99 lakh, 
dispatching eight containers to Gulf countries before exports 
were paused due to geopolitical disruptions.
Avanti Fellows  
Through our partnership with Avanti Fellows, we continued to 
support meritorious yet underprivileged students preparing 
for IIT-JEE and NEET from Jawaharlal Navodaya Schools 
(JNVs). The programme supported 70 students from Grades 
11 and 12, with focused mentoring provided to Grade 12 
students near our Jhagadia factory in Gujarat. In FY 2025–26, 
four students cleared JEE Mains.

Project Saathi
Through Project Saathi, we continued to make significant 
progress in improving contract worker welfare and 
expanding social security coverage across Thermax sites. 
During the year, the initiative expanded from a single state 
in FY 2023–24 to 15 states in India, covering 70 sites across 
TOESL, P&ES (O&M), and select Chemicals locations in 
Gujarat and Chhattisgarh.
We engaged 2,025 contract workers during the year, 
exceeding our annual target of 2,000. More than 300 
physical awareness workshops were conducted to improve 
participation and understanding of government welfare 
schemes. As a result, 2,725 social security benefits were 
facilitated, with over 76% of workers now covered under 
at least one scheme beyond Provident Fund (PF) and  
Employees’ State Insurance Corporation Provident Fund 
(ESIC).
Through digitisation efforts enabled by the SoCo portal, 
we completed socio-economic profiling for approximately 
1,800 workers, generating valuable insights to support 
strategy and planning. We also enhanced the toll-free 
helpline by adding regional language and multimedia 
capabilities, helping resolve over 500 worker queries and 
strengthening engagement.

Thermax’s Decarbonisation Journey
Our decarbonisation journey is anchored in a clear long-term 
vision to reduce our carbon footprint while strengthening 
operational efficiency and resilience. Since establishing 
our baseline in FY 2018–19, we have pursued a structured 
pathway built on energy efficiency, renewable energy 
adoption, green power procurement and a transition to 
cleaner fuels.
This disciplined approach enabled us to surpass our initial 
target of a 25% reduction, achieving a 37% reduction in 
absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon emissions by  
FY 2024–25. Building on this progress, we have set a more 
ambitious target of reducing emissions by 50% by  
FY 2029–30. 
In FY 2025–26, however, our Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 
increased temporarily by 1,703 tCO2 over last year. This 
was primarily due to facility expansions to support business 
growth, increased testing activities, and changes in renewable 
energy procurement regulations. While these factors led to 
a short-term increase in emissions, they do not represent a 
reversal of our decarbonisation journey. Rather, they reflect 
the impact of scaling our operations responsibly while 
renewable energy procurement arrangements evolve.
Our commitment to achieving our FY 2029–30 target remains 
steadfast, supported by continued investments in renewable 
energy, energy efficiency, operational modernisation, and 
cleaner technologies.
Enabling Sustainable Transformation
FY 2025–26 marks a phase of scaling and deepening 
decarbonisation efforts, where multiple site-level initiatives 
collectively contributed to meaningful carbon reduction. 
Across manufacturing facilities, Thermax has accelerated 
the transition towards renewable energy, with increased 
adoption of open access green power, rooftop solar installations, and group captive renewable agreements. 
Our facilities in Paudh, Maharashtra; Sri City, Andhra 
Pradesh; Jhagadia, Gujarat; and Shirwal, Maharashtra, 
have significantly increased their renewable energy share, 
with some locations deriving a substantial portion of their 
energy needs from green sources. At the same time, 
energy efficiency improvements have been embedded into 
operations through process optimisation, automation, and 
equipment upgrades. From compressor optimisation and 
variable frequency drive (VFD) installations to smart digital 
controls and elimination of inefficiencies, these initiatives 
demonstrate a shift towards intelligent energy management 
systems. Equally important has been the transition to cleaner 
fuels, with several facilities moving from conventional fuels 
such as light diesel oil (LDO), liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), 
and high-speed diesel (HSD) to piped natural gas (PNG), 
biomass, and green fuels reducing both carbon emissions 
and operational risks.
Waste Management and Circularity
We continue to strengthen our circular economy approach 
to waste management, with a target of achieving a 5% 
reduction in waste generation by 2030, using FY 2025 as 
the baseline. While waste generation in FY 2025–26 was 
impacted by certain one-time and regulatory factors, 
the underlying trend when adjusted for these influences 
indicates a reduction.
Our strategy focuses on minimising waste through reuse, 
recycling and co-processing, supported by effective source 
segregation, process optimisation and recovery of valuable 
materials. Regular waste audits and employee training 
programmes further reinforce consistent implementation 
across locations.
We maintained waste sent to landfill at 2%, significantly 
below our internal threshold of 5%. Additionally, 12 units are 
now certified as single-use plastic free, and nine units have 
achieved zero waste to landfill certification, reflecting steady 
progress in our sustainable waste management journey.Roadmap till 2030  %

reducing empty container waste, including hazardous 
empty barrel waste. This initiative reflects our 
continued focus on reducing environmental impact 
while enhancing resource efficiency. Biodiversity

Water Stewardship and Effluent 
Management
We continue to pursue responsible water stewardship and 
effective wastewater management across our operations, 
with a target to reduce freshwater consumption by 5% by 
2030, using FY 2025 as the baseline. During FY 2025–26, 
overall water consumption increased by 12.6%, primarily 
due to capacity expansion at Jhagadia and inclusion of the 
Bhiwadi facility. Excluding these factors, water consumption 
across existing operations was only 2% above baseline, 
reflecting stable operational performance.
Our approach to water management remains focused on 
reduction, reuse, recycling and replenishment, supported by 
initiatives such as:
• Reuse of treated wastewater for gardening, flushing 
and cooling 
• Rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge 
• Process optimisation and deployment of water-
efficient technologies 
• Leak detection and prevention programmes 
• Employee engagement and awareness initiatives 
During the year, we harvested 55,650  KL of rainwater and 
reused 2,29,485 KL of treated water across operations. We 
also continued to operate STPs and ETPs across applicable 
locations, with treated water quality monitored through 
National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration 
Laboratories (NABL) accredited laboratories to ensure 
compliance with applicable regulations. Structured water 
audits and initiatives such as the Spot the Leakage campaign 
further strengthened conservation practices across facilities.

Ministry of New and Renewable Energy  
(MNRE): Green Hydrogen
We submitted recommendations to introduce schemes for 
decentralised green hydrogen offtake for industrial use, 
positioning green hydrogen as a key lever for industrial 
decarbonisation. Building on this, the ministry subsequently 
released draft policy guidelines for GH2 under the Strategic 
Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) 
Programme -  Mode 1B (Bring Your Own Buyer) scheme for 
distributed industrial applications. To further accelerate the 
GH2 derivatives market, we then engaged with the ministry 
to help formulate standards for green methanol and green 
ammonia in India. Once these standards are notified, they 
are expected to drive demand for green hydrogen-based 
derivatives and strengthen domestic GH2 consumption. 
Bureau of Energy Efficiency for  
Indian Carbon Markets
We engaged with the bureau to develop two key 
methodologies under the Indian Carbon Markets’ 
voluntary/offset mechanism. These include frameworks 
for compressed biogas plants and biomass-based  
industrial boiler usage, both of which are at advanced  
stages of notification. Upon finalisation, these will enable 
industries to monetise green credits and further advance  
the decarbonisation agenda.Ministry of Heavy Industries, Department of 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
• Withdrawal of Omnibus Technical Regulations (OTR) 
by Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI): We actively 
engaged with MHI to highlight challenges arising from 
the overlap between OTR requirements and existing 
Quality Control Orders (QCOs), impacting material 
procurement, order fulfilment and project execution. 
Through detailed representations of compliance burden 
and testing bottlenecks, we advocated for deferment. 
This resulted in the withdrawal of OTR implementation 
in January 2026, easing supply chain constraints and 
improving policy certainty. 
• QCO Relaxations on Critical Equipment Imports: 
Recognising the time and cost challenges associated 
with QCO compliance, we engaged with the Ministry of 
Commerce and Department of Promotion of Industry 
and Internal Trade (DPIIT). Following sustained 
representation, QCO requirements were withdrawn 
for key component imports such as copper and steel 
between October 2025 and January 2026, supporting 
ease of doing business.

Management Discussion and Analysis
1. Economic Overview 
1.1  Global Economy
The global economy remained resilient but subdued in calendar 
year 2025, with the global growth at 3.4% in 2025 and projecting 
to 3.1% in 2026, and 3.2% in 2027, reflecting slower momentum 
across major economies and continued policy uncertainty.[1]
Inflation continued to moderate from earlier peaks, although 
it remained above comfort levels in several economies due to 
tariff actions, supply chain shifts and renewed energy price 
volatility.[1]
Global trade showed mixed trends during the year. The World 
Trade Organisation (WTO) noted that merchandise trade 
improved in 2025, supported by frontloading of imports ahead 
of tariff changes and strong demand for AI-related goods; 
however, slower growth is expected in 2026.[2]
Investment flows remained under pressure. The United Nations 
Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) reported 
that global FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) declined by 11% to 
USD 1.5 trillion in 2024.[3]
Commodity markets remained an important variable. The World 
Bank expects global commodity prices to ease further, though 
risks remain from geopolitical disruptions.[4]
Labour markets remained stable, with global unemployment 
around 5.0% in 2024 and expected to slightly improve to 4.9% 
in 2026.[5]
The United States remained supported by consumption and 
AI-led investments, while tax changes are expected to influence 
capital expenditure decisions.[6]
China’s growth moderated due to weak demand and real estate 
stress, despite policy support.
Geopolitical risks intensified, particularly in the Middle East, 
contributing to volatility in energy prices and industrial input 
costs.[7]World
